message.content:
It’s hard to name one “best” jazz vocalist—different listeners have different tastes—but here are a few artists most people agree were truly transformative:

| Singer | Why they’re celebrated |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** (Lady Day) | Her phrasing was so intimate it feels like she’s speaking directly into your ear. She turned everyday emotions into timeless songs. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her flawless diction, incredible range, and scat‑sing ability set standards for vocal improvisation. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | With a voice described as a “soprano alto,” she blended bluesy warmth with operatic control, making complex melodies sound effortless. |
| **Nina Simone** | Though often labeled soul or R&B, her deep connection to jazz gave her recordings a haunting, poetic quality that still resonates today. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A modern icon whose husky tone and inventive arrangements keep pushing what jazz singing can do. |

If you want more detail on each artist—or recommendations tailored to a particular era or style—just let me know!
